text: [Crónicas Deportivas](/es/programas/cronicas-deportivas/) París 2024: Oro en levantamiento de potencia y bronce en judo, cosecha de Venezuela en octavo día paralímpico Primera modificación: Escuchar - 02:41 Con el oro en levantamiento de potencia de Clara Fuentes y el bronce en judo de Marcos Blanco, Venezuela suma cuatro medallas en ocho días de competencia en los Juegos Olímpicos de Paris 2024. RFI habló con los protagonistas de la jornada. “Me trae un sentimiento de felicidad y tranquilidad porque se hizo el trabajo. Trabajé mucho para esto. De verdad que siento que todo lo que hice valió la pena”, expresa la venezolana Clara Fuentes al ganar en la categoría de los 50 kilogramos de levantamiento de potencia. Acostada, sube 124 kilos, record paralímpico. Medio día en París, en Caracas apenas madrugan, pero su familia sigue la proeza por televisión por lo que le envían mensajes durante la competencia porque a diferencia de muchos atletas que prefieren, por necesidad apartarse para estar concentrados, el ritual de Clara es mantenerme en contacto con ellos porque “así es como que tal vez baja un poco la presión de la competencia”, asegura. Durante su paso por París 2024 este jueves, recibe mensajes de la cuñada y del tío que le dice lo orgulloso que se siente de ella. Después de escuchar el himno de Venezuela en la Arena La Chapelle, en la que hondean varias banderas de su país, se pasea en silla de ruedas con la medalla de oro. La medalla “pesa un poco, pero la verdad es que la cargo con mucho orgullo, felicidad y me siento muy orgullosa de representar Venezuela y darle esta felicidad para todos”, concluye. Clara Fuentes bate a la representante de China, Xiao Jinping, y a la británica Olivia Broome. Bonce en para judo Al mismo tiempo, su compatriota Marcos Blanco pelea por el bronce en la Arena Champs de Mars, al frente de la Torre Eiffel. Vence con facilidad al indonesio Junaedi (10-0) en la categoría de hasta 60 kilos para judocas ciegos, por lo que explica cómo se sitúa en el tatami para estos combates que son cuerpo a cuerpo. “Es percepción con el movimiento. Uno siente los movimientos y se va guiando de esa manera para poder ejecutar o rechazar algún ataque”, explica Blanco mientras que una gran delegación del gobierno venezolano celebra la victoria. “Me siento bastante contento porque fueron todos estos años de esfuerzo para llegar aquí y poder ganar esa medalla tan anhelada, que estábamos esperando”, explica Marcos que en Tokio 2020 no alcanza a disputar medalla. text: [Los Murciélagos](https://www.eldestapeweb.com/tag/los-murcielagos), la [Selección Argentina](https://www.eldestapeweb.com/tag/seleccion-argentina) masculina de fútbol para ciegos, venció a Brasil por 4 a 3 en la tanda de penales luego de empatar sin goles en el tiempo regular y clasificó a la final de los Juegos Paralímpicos de París 2024. El conjunto albiceleste luchó de igual a igual contra uno de los favoritos del certamen y se impuso en los tiros desde los doce pasos. El sábado enfrentará a Francia, que eliminó a Colombia, en el encuentro por la medalla dorada. Argentina pasó segundo en su grupo tras empatar por 0 a 0 ante Marruecos y Colombia, y ganar en la última fecha ante Japón por la mínima. El combinado dirigido técnicamente por Ariel Figueroa, que tiene al arquero Germán Müleck y a Maximiliano Espinillo como sus máximas figuras, se cruzará con los locales el próximo sábado a partir de las 15 horas para obtener el único título que falta en sus vitrinas: el primer lugar en unos Juegos Paralímpicos. Los Murciélagos cortaron una histórica racha de la Selección de Brasil Este triunfo por penales ante la 'Canarinha', más allá de la histórica rivalidad existente en el fútbol con el país vecino, tiene un condimento especial: la 'Verdeamarelha' nunca había perdido un partido en los Paralímpicos. En las últimas cinco ediciones (Atenas 2004, Pekín 2008, Londres 2012, Rio 2016 y Tokio 2020+1), obtuvieron el oro de manera invicta. El fixture de Los Murciélagos en los Juegos Paralímpicos de París 2024 - Argentina 0-0 Marruecos, domingo 1 de septiembre, 8:30hs. - Argentina 0-0 Colombia, lunes 2 de septiembre, 6:30hs. - Argentina 1-0 Japón, martes 3 de septiembre, 8:30hs. - Argentina 0 (4)-(3) 0 Brasil, jueves 5 de septiembre, 15hs. - Argentina - Francia, sábado 7 de septiembre, 15hs. MÁS INFO Impacto por lo que pasó con Gustavo Fernández en tenis en los Juegos Paralímpicos [Gustavo Fernández](https://www.eldestapeweb.com/tag/gustavo-fernandez), el argentino que es una figura del [tenis](https://www.eldestapeweb.com/tag/tenis) adaptado a nivel mundial, se presentaba en las semifinales de los [Juegos Paralímpicos](https://www.eldestapeweb.com/tag/juegos-paralimpicos) de París 2024 frente al japonés Tokito Oda. El cordobés de 30 años tuvo un gran torneo oficial, como casi siempre, e iba por el boleto a la final para asegurar una nueva medalla para la delegación albiceleste en la capital de Francia. Sin embargo, en el primer set el "Lobito" estuvo lejos de su mejor nivel y cayó por 6-2. Ya en el segundo parcial, inició 3-1 abajo nuevamente, aunque logró equilibrar el marcador y se colocó 3-3. No obstante, el nipón otra vez hizo gala de su jerarquía, se impuso por 7-5 y volvió a dejar en el camino al albiceleste, al igual que en la final del último Roland Garros. Esto no quita el notable trabajo del sudamericano a lo largo del certamen y de la vigente temporada en líneas generales.

text: [Passer au contenu principal](#main) « Ils savent que je suis bon » : Ja'Marr Chase ajoute de l'huile sur le feu Suivez le match entre les Bengals de Cincinnati et les Chiefs de Kansas City dimanche dès 16 h sur RDS2 et RDS.ca. « Ils savent que je suis bon, ils savent comment jouer contre nous. Ce n'est pas comme s'ils avaient de supervedette défensivement. » Avant même de savoir s'il sera en uniforme dimanche contre les Chiefs de Kansas City, le receveur des Bengals de Cincinnati Ja'Marr Chase s'est attaqué à la défense des prochains adversaires de son équipe. Alors que les Bengals jouent leur présence en éliminatoires, Chase a mentionné qu'aucun aspect dans le jeu des secondeurs des Chiefs ne faisait d'eux une menace défensive jeudi. Chase a ensuite ajouté que les champions en titre du Super Bowl n'avaient pas de demi de coin de la trempe de Jalen Ramsey, des Dolphins de Miami. Chase s'en est ensuite pris au demi de sûreté des Chiefs Bryan Cook, présentement blessé, en affirmant qu'il n'était pas comparable à l'ancien demi des Bengals Jessie Bates III. « Je ne fais qu'ajouter de l'huile sur le feu. Ils vont prendre ces commentaires, j'espère qu'ils vont les afficher dans leur vestiaire », a ajouté Chase lorsqu'il s'est fait demander si ses commentaires pouvaient être mal perçus par les Chiefs. Au cours des dernières années, la bataille entre les Bengals et les Chiefs est devenue l'une des plus grandes rivalités de la NFL. En février 2022, les Bengals ont défait Kansas City en finale de l'AFC pour accéder au Super Bowl pour la première fois en plus de trois décennies. Un an plus tard, KC a remporté le match revanche avec un placement sur le dernier jeu de la rencontre. Chase a connu la meilleure rencontre de sa carrière contre les Chiefs. Participant au Pro Bowl dans chacune de ses deux premières saisons dans la NFL, Chase a profité de la semaine 17 en 2021 pour établir un record dans l'histoire des Bengals avec 266 verges de gains de réception. Cincinnati avait triomphé 34-31 pour obtenir son billet pour les éliminatoires. Dans les deux matchs éliminatoires, il a totalisé 12 réceptions, 129 verges de gains et un touché. Chase était un participant limité à l'entraînement jeudi, un signe encourageant pour son retour au jeu puisque c'est la première fois qu'il était impliqué dans les entraînements depuis sa blessure à l'épaule gauche subie contre les Vikings du Minnesota le 16 décembre. « Je me sens bien présentement, j'y vais un jour à la fois », a dit Chase, qui a la décision entre ses mains quant à sa participation au match de dimanche.

text: The Golden State Warriors are reportedly leaving the door open to possibly trading another one of the core members of the 2022 championship-winning team. The Athletic’s Tim Kawakami published an article Thursday that discussed Andrew Wiggins and his fellow wing Jonathan Kuminga, and what the Dubs could possibly do if they can’t coexist. A potential answer is to find a suitable trade partner — for Wiggins. In a “side note,” Kawakami reported that Wiggins’ relatively cheap extension “would not be a major barrier for the Warriors to explore Wiggins’ trade market. Especially if he can’t play with Kuminga and the Warriors decide that Kuminga is their full-time small forward.” Kawakami noted that he had previously believed that the extension — a team-friendly four-year, $109 million deal that was a discount considering the role Wiggins played on a championship team — would stop the Dubs from shopping the 28-year-old forward. Advertisement Article continues below this ad While Wiggins is coming off one of his best games of the season, scoring 22 points on 7-of-11 shooting in a Christmas Day loss to the Nuggets, it’s been a rather rough season for the former No. 1 overall pick. His scoring and offensive production have been down across the board, and ESPN’s Kendra Andrews reported last month that Warriors were “annoyed” with his poor conditioning heading into this season. Seeing Kuminga come into form this season could very well indicate to the front office that it’s time to accelerate the end of Wiggins’ tenure with the Warriors. At the same time, it’s difficult to say for sure if the team has to move on from the Canadian wing. As Kawakami noted, whether Wiggins stays or goes depends on how he meshes within different Golden State lineups. That’s a hard thing for the team to get a proper sense of with Draymond Green currently on an indefinite suspension. The Jordan Poole trade this offseason was a sign that being a pivotal member of the Warriors’ last championship team wasn’t enough to prevent a trade. text: Arteta classifica derrota do Arsenal como "decepcionante" e despista sobre novos reforços Nesta quinta-feira, o Arsenal desperdiçou a chance de reassumir a liderança da Premier League. Pela 19ª rodada, os Gunners foram derrotados pelo West Ham, em casa, por 2 a 0. Os mandantes acumularam 30 finalizações contra o adversário, e, por isso, o técnico Mikel Arteta classificou o resultado como "decepcionante". "Quero parabenizar o West Ham e elogiar meus jogadores, é só isso que posso dizer. Isso é o futebol. Você vê o que fizemos durante o jogo, como criamos… e o resultado é decepcionante, mas eles foram melhores que nós em ambas as áreas. Eles tiveram dois chutes no gol, três se contar o pênalti, e nós tivemos 30", afirmou o espanhol em coletiva pós-jogo. Arteta ainda complementou: "No futebol, você precisa fazer isso melhor (finalizar) se quiser vencer. Hoje, não ganhamos por conta disso. De resto, o time continuou tentando e teve uma ótima atitude novamente". O comandante dos Gunners também disse que acredita que a má fase do ataque não esteja relacionada à falta de confiança dos atletas. "Você chuta na trave, ou você finaliza e a bola não entra por meio centímetro, ou alguém bloqueia o chute e a bola não entra. Também perdemos muitas oportunidades na escolha do último passe. Isso faz a diferença para vencer os jogos". Quando questionado se o Arsenal iria atrás de algum jogador para resolver os problemas de conversão de chances, o treinador despistou e deixou claro que está feliz com o elenco que tem em mãos. "O que temos são estes jogadores, e são estes atletas que eu amo muito. O que temos que fazer é nos colocarmos em situações melhores e treinar mais. Temos que colocá-los lá e aumentar a confiança deles, porque eles já fizeram grandes coisas", concluiu. O Arsenal foi ultrapassado pelo Liverpool, que venceu e alcançou 42 pontos no Inglês. Com 40, o time de Londres terminou a rodada na segunda colocação. O próximo desafio da equipe de Arteta será neste domingo, às 11 horas (de Brasília), contra o Fulham, em Craven Cottage. 💬 "We have to learn from it and make sure we get sharper and better in front of the goals." text: The Detroit Pistons historic losing streak extended to 28-straight games and counting after they suffered a 128-122 overtime loss to the Boston Celtics . To add insult injury the Pistons blew a 21-point they accumulated during the second quarter to tie the longest losing streak in NBA history. Detroit's shocking streak had given them sole possession of the NBA record for the longest season single streak in league history on Tuesday following a defeat to the Brooklyn Nets . Detroit's embarrassing loss to the Celtics now ties the mark set by the Philadelphia 76ers during a losing run that spanned the 2014-15 season to the 2015-16 seasons. 'I'm unbelievably proud of the group, the way they bring it,' Pistons head coach Monty Williams said. The Pistons blew a 21-point first half lead against the Celtics to extent their losing streak Detroit is now tied for the longest-ever losing streak in NBA history with the 76ers at 28 games Celtics center Kristaps Porzingis led the game with 35 points and fueled Boston's win 'They've heard all the stuff about our team and they just keep bringing it. I know it's going to pay off.' Detroit was able to jump out to a massive advantage early on and led by 19 points as the game entered halftime. Their lead had reached as high as 21 points during the first half. Things took an unbelievable turn during the third quarter however, after the Celtics were able to battle back and tie things up at 82-82 heading into the fourth quarter thanks to a 23-7 run. Pistons superstar guard Cade Cunningham followed up his tremendous 41-point performance in Tuesday's historic loss by scoring a team-high 31 as Detroit tried to win game since October 28. 'I'm not interested in just winning one more game this year -- you know what I mean? To stop this. That would be soft, in my opinion,' said Cunningham. 'Our goals are a lot higher than that. We have what it takes to win a game, that's nothing. But to put games together, to find our system, find what's clicking and allow us to sustain winning. That's all we're looking for.' Cunnigham had picked up an incredible 22 points during the first half alone before finishing the game with his grand totals of 31 pts, nine assists, and six rebounds. 'We're on the same level as all these teams were playing against,' said Cunningham. 'There's no team that I've ever come across in the NBA where I felt like I was going into a slaughterhouse. I've never felt like that in my life, going into a basketball game. 'So every game we should be able to fight teams and impose our will on them. We did that early on. We kind of let go of the rope a little bit in the third quarter. But there's a lot of growth, and something we can learn from and definitely take to the next game.' Boston on the other hand were led by center Kristaps Porzingis who ended the night with a game-high 35 pts, eight rebounds, and eight assists. Celtics small forward Jayson Tatum ended the game with 31 pts, 10 asts, eight rebs, and five steals to pick up one of his most important double-doubles on the season. Cade Cunningham led the Pistons effort and scored a team-high 31 points during the loss Pistons coach Monty Williams was 'unbelievably proud of the group, the way they bring it' The game was nearly decided in the final seconds when Cunningham was called for a goaltending violation with 8.7 seconds left as Tatum attempted a shot to break a 106-106 tie and give the Celtics a two-point advantage. Pistons forward Bojan Bogdanovic was able to secure a put back layup with less than five seconds left to force the game into overtime. After overtime guard Derrick White began playing like a man possessed to ensure the Celtics avoided an embarrassing loss on their home court. White ended the night with 23 points. Detroit's next chance to end their losing ways will be on Saturday night against the Toronto Raptors. If the Pistons suffer another loss against Toronto, it will give them sole possession of the longest losing streak in NBA history at 29 games.

text: Ja’Marr Chase is doing everything he can to rile up the Chiefs’ defense — and the Bengals wide receiver may not even be on the field come New Year’s Eve. Chase had plenty to say about Kansas City’s defense on Thursday, none of which was particularly nice. Specifically, he took shots at the Chiefs’ secondary, saying that there was “nothing” that stood out about them. “They could take it how they [want to take it]. I don’t care,” Chase told reporters, according to NFL.com . But it didn’t stop there. When Chase, 23, was asked about Chiefs safety and Cincinnati native Bryan Cook, the Bengals wide receiver was far from complimentary. “I don’t even know who that is,” Chase said. “Is that No. 6? I don’t know, man. Just a guy to me. He ain’t Jessie Bates to me. You want me to go [into] comparisons? It’s not the same. Just saying.” And even when the two-time Pro Bowler seemed to finally pay someone on the Chiefs’ defense a compliment, it would still best described as backhanded. He called cornerback L’Jarius Sneed “the best player” on Kansas City, but not without adding that their other defensive backs aren’t on the same level as Sneed. “That’s why they double everybody, because they can’t do it one on one,” Chase said. Though Chase didn’t seem to have an issue speaking frankly about the Bengals’ upcoming opponent, he may not be on the field to answer for his words. Chase was sidelined for last week’s loss to the Steelers due to a separated shoulder, and he was only a limited participant during Thursday’s practice. The Bengals are still in the playoff hunt, and Chase wants to play, but it isn’t a guarantee he will suit up. Cincinnati will be up against a desperate Chiefs team that has dropped five of its last seven games and is frustrated with the turn of events . Chase’s words aren’t likely to sit well with the Chiefs or their fans, but he showed little concern for that. “I’m just adding fire to the fuel right now,” Chase said. “They’re gonna take this and run with it. Hope they put it in their locker. It’s alright, though. As long as I’m mentally ready to play.” The Bengals have defeated the Chiefs in three of their last four meetings.

text: Fahad Shabbir (@FahadShabbir) Published September 06, 2024 | 01:40 AM Paris, (APP - UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News - 6th Sep, 2024) Japan won their first gold medal in the men's goalball via golden goal at the Paralympics on Thursday, while Turkey claimed their third consecutive title in the women 's event . Sano Yuto scored the golden goal to give Japan victory against Ukraine by four goals to three after extra time in the South Paris Arena, marking a strong improvement on their fifth-placed finish at their home Games three years ago. In front of a capacity crowd, Japan broke the deadlock through Kazuya Kaneko and Koji Miyajiki to take a 2-0 lead inside the opening three minutes. But Ukraine struck back, first via Anton Strelchyk and then through a Vasyl Oliinyk penalty, to level the score going into the break. Japan came within inches of retaking the lead two minutes into the second period, only for Ukraine 's Oleksandr Toporkov to charge back and grab the ball right on the line. They did soon restore their lead in a tense second half, however, when Sano powered a throw through the Ukrainian defence to make it 3-2 to the Japanese. Ukraine tried to force the issue but the solid black-and-red wall Japan 's trio had constructed in front of their goal held fast until two minutes from time. Strelchyk's throw was only half-parried away and the ball squirmed into the goal to make it 3-3, forcing extra time. Yuto then fired in the winning goal to spark wild celebrations as Japan became Paralympic champions for the first time. - Turkish delight - After tasting gold at Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020 , the Turkish women 's team have now won gold in all three of the appearances at the Paralympics following their 8-3 victory over Israel . "Three finals, three championships, three gold medals," said Turkey 's triple Paralympic champion Sevda Altunoluk. "I can't explain my feelings because I am so happy and the feeling is so deep." Reigning world champions Turkey made a fast start against Israel in the final, scoring two goals inside the first two minutes, courtesy of Altunoluk and Fatma Gul Guler. Israel called for a time-out just after Turkey 's third and then immediately struck back through Lihi Ben David to make it 3-1. However, a team penalty against Israel , which was duly converted by Guler, and another goal seconds later from Altunoluk pushed Turkey further ahead. The Turks added two more goals before Ben David doubled up to take the sides into half-time with the score at 7-2. The second period started cagily until Altunoluk scored with a fine cross-court effort that flew into the bottom corner. Israel 's Ben David got her third with just under five minutes to go but Turkey were home and dry. Turkey 's Altunoluk finished top-scorer of the gold medal match on four goals and 21 for the whole tournament. In the bronze medal matches, China 's women eased past Brazil 6-0 to claim bronze , while in the same fixture on the men's side of the draw Brazil beat the Chinese 5-3.

text: A’ja Wilson is a frontrunner to take home this season’s WNBA MVP honor — the award would be her third after winning it in 2020 and 2022 — and she’s doing so in style. Wilson’s performance during the Las Vegas Aces’ game against the Atlanta Dream on Friday, August 30 is a perfect example of her ability to take over the court and look good while doing it. For the Friday match-up, Wilson wore a special version of LeBron James’ Nike LeBron 21 sneaker in a player exclusive colorway. Wilson’s PE was inspired by her sorority, Alpha Kappa Alpha, which she joined while attending the University of South Carolina. With a mostly black upper, Wilson’s Alpha Kappa Alpha-inspired LeBron 21 PEs added accents of the sorority’s colors, salmon pink and apple green. Salmon pink filled the shoe’s Swoosh and Air Zoom-cushioned midsole, while the apple green color was more subtly used on the eyelets, tongue logo and the heel’s detailing. Understated yet elegant, the exclusive pair didn’t appear to feature any official Alpha Kappa Alpha branding, but the colors were enough to tell the story. A’ja Wilson (left) guards Laeticia Amihere of the Atlanta Dream during an August 30 game. Credit: Getty Alpha Kappa Alpha was founded at Howard University in 1908 and is recognized as the first intercollegiate historically Black sorority. It boasts a number of notable members, among them is presidential nominee Kamala Harris. Wilson and Harris shared a sorority-related moment together in August 2023 during the Aces’ visit to the White House after winning the ’22 WNBA championship. @wnba VP, Kamala Harris, had to drop @A’ja Wilson some #AKA love real quick at the @Las Vegas Aces White House visit 💚🩷 #wnba #whitehousevisit ♬ original sound – WNBA Wilson attended the University of South Carolina from 2014 to 2018, where she was a member of AKA’s Theta Gamma chapter. She earned numerous SEC accolades in college before being drafted first overall by the Aces in the 2018 WNBA Draft. Her WNBA career has been illustrious, with many regarding her as a top active player today. In addition to her aforementioned MVP honors, she led the Aces to WNBA championships in ’22 and ’23. In the summer of 2024, Wilson propelled the US women’s Olympic basketball team to their eighth straight gold medal. Wilson’s debut signature sneaker, the Nike A’One , will be released in 2025. text: Nigerian defender, Olisa Ndah, who currently plays for South African club Orlando Pirates, has expressed his openness to making a move to Europe. The 26-year-old centre-back has been a key player for Orlando since joining from Akwa United, a team in the Nigeria Professional Football League, in 2021. Ndah has helped his team win the MTN 8 League Cup in two consecutive seasons at the Orlando Stadium in Soweto. Despite his strong individual performances and consistency, a rumored transfer to Italian club Sassuolo never materialized as no official bid was made. However, Ndah remains optimistic about a potential move to Europe. He emphasized his satisfaction with his current role at Orlando Pirates but admitted he is open to new opportunities should they arise. “I’m happy where I am, but I’m open to any opportunity that comes my way,” Ndah told Goal in an interview. Ndah began his professional career in the Nigeria Professional Football League with Remo Stars during the 2018/2019 season. After 18 months, he joined Akwa United, where he won the league title. Since 2021, Ndah has been playing in South Africa with Orlando Pirates and continues to aim for a future move to Europe.

text: Table of Contents Toggle McCullum’s Vision for English Cricket New Leadership Structure McCullum’s Trust in Stokes Future Expectations Stokes’ Aspirations McCullum’s Confidence in Team Performance Support for Buttler Looking Ahead Debut for Hull McCullum’s Vision for English Cricket Brendon McCullum has voiced his expectation that Ben Stokes will be completely dedicated to the England cricket team following the New Zealander’s contract extension, which now includes the management of both Test and limited-overs formats. New Leadership Structure After taking the helm as head coach two years ago, McCullum, 42, has made significant changes to England’s Test cricket approach. He will now also lead the white-ball teams starting in January. Stokes, 33, who serves as the Test captain, had previously come out of retirement to participate in the one-day international setup during last year’s World Cup, although he has not been part of England’s white-ball squad since then. McCullum’s Trust in Stokes Regarding their working relationship, McCullum stated, “He’s been incredible and our relationship is fantastic. You never know where the game’s going globally and what sort of opportunities will pop up for him, but I know how invested he is in English cricket and how determined he is to drive this team forward.” Future Expectations Before McCullum’s recent extension of his contract, there were speculations about both he and Stokes potentially stepping down after the upcoming Ashes series in Australia planned for the winter of 2025-26. However, under the new agreement, McCullum will retain leadership until the home Ashes in the summer of 2027 along with the 50-over World Cup scheduled for later that year. His tenure will see him involved in the Champions Trophy early in the coming year and a T20 World Cup in 2026. Stokes’ Aspirations In a recent interview with the Telegraph, Stokes expressed that “in an ideal world” he would still hold the position of Test captain in 2027, indicating that he finds it challenging to decline participation in global tournaments. McCullum’s Confidence in Team Performance In anticipation of the upcoming Test match against Sri Lanka at the Kia Oval, McCullum remarked, “The skipper and I haven’t spoken, but I’m assuming he’s all in. He seems like that sort of bloke.” He further expressed confidence in Stokes’ ability to thrive in high-pressure situations. Support for Buttler McCullum also affirmed his support for Jos Buttler as England’s white-ball captain, despite a tough year that culminated in the departure of coach Matthew Mott. Despite England’s recent struggles, having lost significantly in the 50-over World Cup and semi-finals of the T20 World Cup, McCullum remains optimistic about Buttler’s contributions. He described Buttler’s demeanor as occasionally “a little bit miserable at times,” urging him to enjoy the forthcoming years and seize the opportunity to lead a talented group of players. Looking Ahead With the packed schedule for England’s cricket team, McCullum indicated that he would miss some series, delegating responsibilities to assistant coaches while balancing time with his family in New Zealand. Having achieved victories in all five Tests this summer, England is aiming for a clean sweep against Sri Lanka this week—a feat they haven’t accomplished since 2004. Debut for Hull The team is set to introduce Leicestershire’s left-arm bowler Josh Hull, selecting him based on potential despite a challenging domestic record. McCullum noted, “What we are trying to achieve is bringing in some of these guys who we see as rough diamonds with incredibly high ceilings.” Despite uncertainty regarding the schedule for their upcoming Tests in Pakistan, McCullum expressed hope for clarity soon so that team selections can proceed smoothly.

text: Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick have been labelled as "spoiled brats" over their recent performances. The criticism came from none other than Chiefs legend Dante Hall, who despite his relationship with the pair, did not hold back with his criticism. "It's like my little kids running around here on Christmas Day," the 45-year-old said on 'Good Morning Football' . "We got you a Christmas tree filled with presents, and you're acting like spoiled little brats. These guys know I love them. "So, as a friend, as a brother, I had to call you out. Get back to being positive and not so negative on the sideline with your guys. Be better and I think the team will be better." text: Mikel Arteta admitted his side came up short in both boxes as Arsenal slumped to defeat against West Ham to miss out on regaining top spot in the Premier League. text: Angola netted a late strike to secure a shock 1-0 win against Black Stars of Ghana in their first game in Group F of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers in Kumasi on Thursday. The defeat was a big blow to Ghana’s long-standing dominance at the Baba Yara Stadium, ending the Black Stars’ 24-year unbeaten home record there. Felicio Milson emerged as the hero for Angola, scoring a dramatic 93rd-minute goal that not only secured the win but also shocked the home crowd. Despite Ghana controlling much of the game, Milson’s late strike from close range after Ghanaian defender Abdul Mumin cleared the ball into his path sealed the upset. The other two teams that make up Group F alongside Ghana and Angola are Niger Republic and Sudan. In their own opening fixture, Sudan also secured a 1-0 home win against Niger Republic. Coach Otto Addo and his players would hope to bounce back from the disappointing home loss when they will be guests to Niger on Monday, September 9th.

text: Padres Encouraged by Yu Darvish's Return, Despite 'Rust' Yu Darvish is back. In a [season filled with adversity](https://www.si.com/mlb/padres/san-diego-padres-news/padres-could-be-without-yu-darvish-for-extended-period-01j281pmzzsk) for the starting pitcher, Darvish only had 11 games this season under his belt before returning to the mound Wednesday. The 38-year-old right-hander had not appeared in a major league game since May 29 until his first pitch Wednesday against the Detroit Tigers. Although Darvish didn't figure into the Padres’ 6-5 victory, the team was happy to have him back. The 2021 National League All-Star logged a 3.51 ERA, allowing four hits, three runs, and one home run across 2.2 innings. He struck out four batters and walked two. “There was a lot of adrenaline going into this game, maybe a little trying to do too much, kind of getting used to the pitch clock again,” Darvish said to [The Athletic’s Dennis Lin.](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5746369/2024/09/05/yu-darvish-padres-return-il/) “I think a key (going forward) would be to try to be a little bit calmer.” Darvish’s unimpressive final line (2.2 innings, three runs, all earned) saw his ERA for the season jump to 3.51. But Padres manager Mike Shildt was satisfied with Darvish’s performance. He understands the newly returned pitcher needs time to get back into the groove of the major leagues. “The stuff was great,” Shildt [ said to Lin](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5746369/2024/09/05/yu-darvish-padres-return-il/). “It was coming out easy. The secondary pitches looked like they were there. As you can expect the first game back in a big-league game, it was a little bit of just missing either off (the plate) or just missing too much on. Command does speak for itself, but I thought the ball came out well. He said he felt good. His arm felt good. His body felt good. Just knocked a little bit of the proverbial rust off. But I was really encouraged by how it was coming out.” The addition of Darvish into the Padres’ rotation will be beneficial as the team prepares for the postseason. Before Darvish returned, San Diego had major question marks outside its top four starters — Dylan Cease, Michael King, Joe Musgrove, and Martín Pérez. Second-year pitcher Randy Vasquez had been shuffling in and out of the fifth starter's spot amid Darvish's absence. While he gave the Padres a chance to win on most nights, Vasquez was also terribly inconsistent. In his last outing before being optioned to Triple-A, the right-hander allowed 11 hits and nine runs in 4.1 innings against the Tampa Bay Rays. Across the 11 games Darvish pitched before his hiatus, he accrued a 3.20 ERA while throwing 53 strikeouts and 15 walks. “You give a guy three months off basically, and he’s doing what he can to get back and healthy, and obviously, he grinded to do it. It’s not easy," Padres outfielder Jackson Merrill [ said to Lin](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5746369/2024/09/05/yu-darvish-padres-return-il/). "Getting him now at the strength he has and how healthy he is, it’s huge for us.” With his return, Darvish will serve as an additional reliable starter for the Padres' rotation.

text: LLOR BLIMEY Tottenham legend Hugo Lloris closing in on transfer exit after being axed as captain by Ange Postecoglou Frenchman has not featured in a matchday squad under Ange Postecoglou Posted Friday, December 29, 2023 by Thesun.co.uk HUGO LLORIS is in advanced talks over a move to MLS outfit Los Angeles FC. The former France captain, who turned 37 on Boxing Day, has been at Tottenham for 11 years. Hugo Lloris is set to leave Tottenham after over a decade in North London Credit: PA But he has not featured at all this season following the signing of goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario from Empoli in June. He had options to leave in the summer but snubbed interest from Lazio, Newcastle, former club Nice and Saudi Arabia. Yet Lloris looks close to ending his stay in North London by moving Stateside to LAFC, the club where former Spurs team-mate Gareth Bale finished his career. Lloris’s deal is up in the summer but him moving now would be a boost to Tottenham’s wage kitty as he is on more than £100,000 a week. He racked up a whopping 447 appearances for Spurs although sadly his last one was the infamous 6-1 defeat at Newcastle in April, when he came off injured at half-time having shipped five goals. Injury-hit Spurs will lose captain Son Heung-min to the Asian Cup next month as well as midfielders Yves Bissouma and Pape Sarr to the African Cup of Nations. Yet more players could still leave with Eric Dier regularly overlooked by boss Ange Postecoglou, who has prioritised signing a new centre-back in January. Pierre Emile-Hojbjerg could also leave having fallen down the pecking order under Postecoglou, but would likely be replaced Postecoglou recently heaped praise upon Lloris, saying: "[His future] is not my decision. It’s a decision for Hugo and the club. I don’t have that power and don’t want that power. "Hugo is a member of this squad and how he trains every day is important to me. If he wasn’t then I’d be dealing with it but I haven’t had to, he has been absolutely first-class. “As a manager, I don’t take that for granted because that could be a problem for me. For most managers, it is the ones who aren’t playing who give you the biggest headaches. It’s his decision to make." text: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Elijah Moore is being evaluated for a concussion after a scary injury in the second quarter Thursday night. He hit the turf hard after catching a pass from Joe Flacco , and he immediately headed the blue medical tent with some help. Moore was having a big game at the time of his injury, hauling in five receptions for 61 yards and a touchdown. After spending some time in the tent, he walked back to the Cleveland locker room for further evaluation. Moore is having a career year in his first season with the Browns. He had new career-highs in receptions (54) and yards (579), but only had one touchdown to his name. He spent the last two years with the Jets before making his way to Cleveland. The Browns were down a key playmaker for Thursday night’s matchup. Wide receiver Amari Cooper appeared to tweak his injury during warmups, and he was ruled out as a result. That meant Moore and others would have to step up. If he’s unable to go, though, it’ll be next man up for Cleveland. With Joe Flacco at QB, Browns are rolling with playoffs approaching The Browns have put together an impressive stretch lately since Flacco took the reins at quarterback. They entered Thursday’s game 3-1 with the former Baltimore Raven under center, and quickly took control against the struggling Jets. Cleveland struck first when Flacco found Jerome Ford for a 7-yard touchdown and found pay dirt again when Kareem Hunt ran in a score. After Hickman’s pick-six, the Browns added to their lead again when Flacco hit Elijah Moore for a touchdown to make it a 27-7 lead in the second quarter. It was all Cleveland in the first half as the Browns took a 34-17 lead into halftime — and, you could say, it was an elite start for Flacco. He completed 16 of 22 passes for 296 yards and three touchdowns through the first two quarters. Entering Thursday night, Flacco was averaging more than 325 yards per game and his only loss came against the Los Angeles Rams in his first game with the Browns. Then, Cleveland started its three-game win streak with a 31-26 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Browns followed that up with a 20-17 comeback victory over the Chicago Bears behind 374 yards from Flacco. With a talented defense, things are getting interesting in Cleveland as fans start to set their sights on a possible playoff appearance. The Browns entered TNF as the No. 5 seed in the AFC.

text: CBV mantém Zé Roberto e Bernardinho no comando das seleções de vôlei José Roberto Guimarães, Bernardinho e Leandro Brachola continuarão à frente de suas respectivas modalidades. A Confederação Brasileira de Vôlei (CBV) anunciou nesta quinta-feira, por meio de seu site, a manutenção de todos os técnicos das seleções de vôlei profissionais, visando o ciclo olímpico de Los Angeles 2028. Após reuniões que contaram com a presença do presidente Radamés Lattari e do diretor técnico Jorge Bichara, ficou definido que José Roberto Guimarães, Bernardinho e Leandro Brachola continuarão no comando das seleções de vôlei de quadra e de praia. Bernardinho, treinador brasileiro que mais vezes subiu ao pódio olímpico, com seis medalhas conquistadas, continuará à frente da seleção masculina de vôlei de quadra, enquanto José Roberta Guimarães, que tem cinco medalhas, seguirá no comando da seleção feminina. Ambos os treinadores também seguirão exercendo a função de coordenador técnico de suas respectivas modalidades. Este cargo foi criado em 2023 para reforçar a integração entre as seleções adultas e de base. Leandro Brachola, coordenador técnico do vôlei de praia no último ciclo, onde Duda e Ana Patrícia conquistaram o ouro em Paris, também aceitou dar continuidade ao trabalho na Seleção Brasileira.

text: [Passer au contenu principal](#main) Édouard Julien propulse les Twins avec son 1er circuit depuis avril Édouard Julien a frappé un circuit de trois points et les Twins du Minnesota ont battu les Rays de Tampa Bay 4-3, jeudi. La claque de Julien a ouvert la marque en deuxième manche. Il s'agit de son huitième circuit de la saison, son premier depuis le 25 avril. Matt Wallner a ajouté un circuit en solo en troisième. Les deux circuits ont été accordés par Taj Bradley (6-10), qui a été excellent pour le reste de son départ, terminant sa journée de travail avec quatre points mérités sur six coups sûrs avec dix retraits sur des prises en sept manches. Bradley présente une fiche de 0-6 à ses sept derniers départs. Le jeu a été interrompu pendant 13 minutes en raison d'une révision vidéo en septième. Avec un pointage de 4-2 Twins et Jonny DeLuca au troisième but, Yandy Diaz a frappé la balle en flèche vers le coin au champ droit. Wallner a saisi la balle après deux bonds pendant que DeLuca croisait le marbre avant de terminer sa course dans l'enclot des caméramans. Les arbitres se sont consultés pendant de longues minutes pour finalement déterminer que Diaz devait se retrouver au deuxième. Griffin Jax a alors été appelé en relève à Pablo Lopez (14-8) et il a préservé l'avance d'un point des Twins en forçant Brandon Lowe à frapper un roulant. Lopez a accordé trois points sur sept coups sûrs avec neuf retraits au bâton en six manches et deux tiers. Jhoan Duran a été parfait en neuvième manche pour enregistrer un 22e sauvetage en 24 tentatives. Les Twins (76-64) ont pris une avance d'un demi-match devant les Royals de Kansas City (76-65) pour la deuxième place des équipes repêchées de l'Américaine. Junior Caminero a réussi un simple de deux points pour les Rays, en troisième manche. Ailleurs dans la MLB Astros 0 - Reds 1 HOU : Hunter Brown n'a pas accordé de point en six manches au monticule. Les Astros ont subi leur 1er balayage depuis avril. CIN : Rhett Lowder a blanchi les Astros pendant six manches et un tiers et Ty France a claqué un circuit en solo en 7e. text: Pablo López on point as Twins earn series split with Rays Edouard Julien and Matt Wallner homered for the offense as the Twins split a four-game series with a 4-3 victory ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Fresh off an ugly defensive game on Wednesday, and digesting tough injury news about Byron Buxton, who will be delayed in his return, and Max Kepler, who landed on the injured list, the Twins needed someone who could send them to Kansas City for a pivotal series against the Royals with some optimism. And who better than Pablo López? ADVERTISEMENT López has looked every bit the ace in the second half of the season and on Thursday, he helped lead the Twins to a 4-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays in the series finale at Tropicana Field. “The team picked me up plenty of times in the first half when I wasn’t at my best or my sharpest,” López said. “It’s one of those things that you have to take it personal. We were down in the series and I knew I had an opportunity to come out here and do it for my guys, for my teammates.” His 23⅓-scoreless innings streak was broken in the third inning when he allowed a two-run single to top prospect Junior Caminero, but the right-hander featured some of his best stuff as the Twins (76-64) salvaged a split of the four-game series. López threw three different pitches above 98 mph, including one at 98.6 — the hardest pitch of his career. And his sweeper had a 70 percent whiff rate, accounting for seven of the 18 swinging strikes he racked up in the game. ADVERTISEMENT “As well as he’s been throwing the ball, this may have been as good of a day with some of his best stuff we’ve seen literally in two years,” bench coach Jayce Tingler said. He gave up just one other run in the game, in the seventh inning when Yandy Díaz doubled to right. Matt Wallner tracked down the ball and his momentum took him tumbling over the outfield wall. A lengthy rules review followed as the umpires figured out which base to place Díaz on. More than 10 minutes had passed, likely leading to the of López’s day as Griffin Jax was summoned to finish off the seventh inning. ADVERTISEMENT López said he was a little frustrated because one of the few fastballs he yanked in the game went for a double and then the delay took much longer than he expected. “I was hoping to stay in the game after that, just to give me an opportunity to end on a better note by getting that last out,” López said. “But didn’t win that conversation. The best reliever in baseball came to get that last out.” Though he didn’t get that final 21st out that he was hoping for, it was yet again another promising start from López when his team needed him the most. And it comes as no surprise to those around him. ADVERTISEMENT “We know how hard he works. We know how good his stuff is. It felt like it was just a tick off (earlier this season). text: Australian long-jumper Vanessa Low shatters world record in Paris Paralympics triumph Australian long-jumper Vanessa Low has completed a Paralympic threepeat, winning gold at Stade de France on Friday morning AEST. The 34-year-old, who also took home gold at Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020, jumped 5.45m in the women’s long jump T63 competition to topple her own world record of 5.33m, achieve in Canberra earlier this year. Her closest competitor, silver medallist Martina Carboni of Italy, recorded a best distance of 5.06m, while Switzerland’s Elena Kratter claimed bronze. “I love putting myself on the big stage, and I think I can jump six metres,” Low said. “I think this is my next big goal, six is possible, I want to break down barriers. “When I first picked up the sport we were at 4.5m and now we are all pushing boundaries.” Elsewhere in Paris, Australian swimmer Tim Hodge won his first individual Paralympic gold medal after placing first in the men’s 200m individual medley SM9 final with a time 2:13.31. The 23-year-old, who also won gold in the mixed 4x100m medley relay 34 Points earlier this week, toppled the Paralympic record that was set by fellow Australian Matthew Cowdrey in 2008. Frence duo Ugo Didier and Hector Denayer joined Hodge on the podium. “When I told that to my parents they were adamant, no, we’ll find something that I was good at,” Hodge said. “It was something they worked their whole lives to give me the best opportunities and find what I was good at. “I am extremely proud to say that all the hard times and everything was worth it.” Before arriving in the French capital, Hodge had two Paralympic silver medals and a bronze to his name, each achieved in Tokyo three years ago.

text: World champion Sha'Carri Richardson went some way to avenging her Olympic defeat by Julien Alfred by reversing the tables in the 100m at the Diamond League meet in Zurich on Thursday. Richardson headed into the final 20 metres at the Letzigrund Stadium in third behind Saint Lucia's Olympic champion Alfred and Britain's Dina Asher-Smith. But the American stayed strong and focused on the line, producing a savage dip for first place in 10.84 seconds, 0.04sec ahead of Alfred. "I am training and executing because I know the race is not going to take care of itself," said Richardson. Asher-Smith, who failed to make the 100m final in the French capital, rounded out the podium in 10.89sec. Alfred had no complaints about the result, saying the race "felt good". "I am just having fun. I am trying to finish strong. I really have not had the chance to take my medal in," she said. "After Paris I went back to Texas, did some training. It has been up and down, I am still working on the fine tuning." Alfred's gold in Paris was the first-ever Olympic medal of any colour for her tiny Caribbean island homeland. And she said she was now looking to the Diamond League finls in Brussels next week and then returning home for some proper celebrations. "In Brussels I will not run the double, just the 100m," she said. "My aim is nothing in particular, just to finish strong. I am looking forward to go to Saint Lucia, just to celebrate with my country." lp/jc/ea

text: Governing bodies should have their funding cut if they fail to protect female sports amid concern about trans- gender players, a leading think-tank says. A report by the Policy Exchange warns that gender ideology is risking the fairness and safety of competitions for women and girls. The analysis, which is backed by athletes including Martina Navratilova, Sharron Davies and Daley Thompson, highlights the major physical advantages which biological males have over females. The winning woman at this year's London Marathon would have been beaten by the 231st ranked male, it found. And every British 'long course' swimming record set by an elite female swimmer has been beaten by a teenage boy. In addition, at least three female records set at 5k community Parkrun events are held by biological males. Martina Navratilova of the USA takes part in the Legends All Access Hour at the Australian Open tennis tournament at Melbourne Park in Melbourne, Australia, in 2020 Sharron Davies at the Beauty Awards in London, in 2019 The report highlighted concerns about 'gender self-ID', saying it 'fundamentally compromises fair and safe competition for women and girls within grassroots, amateur and elite sport'. Policy Exchange is now calling on sport governing bodies, the UK Government and the International Olympic Committee to restrict categories for women and girls to biological females at all levels of sport. Some 99.99 per cent of those taking part in sport and physical activity are not elite or professional, the report points out, meaning that grassroots competitions for females are 'much more likely' to be affected by the issue. In county athletics championships, the winning male from the slowest county in the 1,500m race in 2023 would have beaten the winning female in 27 out of 33 counties, the think-tank said. It recommends that the Department for Culture, Media and Sport should require all national governing bodies to update their policies within 12 months to ensure that there is a protected female single-sex category – and that they should lose taxpayer funding if they fail to do so. Policy Exchange also says that Parkrun should be ordered to collect participant data based on biological sex and not gender identity, and update all relevant course records to reflect this within 12 months or lose tax- payer funding. Former Olympic swimmer Ms Davies said: 'There is a sense within sports policy that while we should protect the female category within elite sports, women and girls participating and competing at amateur levels should budge over. Former British decathlete Daley Thompson at the Laureus World Sports Awards ceremony at the Verti Music Hall in Berlin, Germany, in 2020 'They must 'be kind' and 'inclusive' while having to pretend it is not grossly unfair, demotivating and possibly unsafe to accommodate biological males within their races, teams and sports days. 'Every sport, at every level, from grassroots to elite, must ensure that the female category is ringfenced for biological females.' Ms Navratilova, the former world No 1 female tennis player and an 18-time grand slam champion, said: 'Female sport must be protected otherwise we risk not only alienating a generation of women, but also taking away dreams and possibilities of fairness and winning for girls and women.' Daley Thompson, two-time Olympic gold medallist in the decathlon, said: 'We risk alienating a generation of young female athletes if we cannot promise them fair and safe play from the grassroots level to the top. 'Categories exist to allow everyone the chance to participate, and the willingness to compromise this by policymakers within sport is a scandal.' A spokesman for Sport England, which is responsible for developing grassroots sport, said: 'In 2021, the Sports Council Equality Group published Transgender Inclusion in Domestic Sport Guidance. While it is up to sports to set their own rules, we work closely with all organisations we fund to ensure they meet all the agreed criteria and code for sports governance. 'In this challenging and emotive area of policy, we understand and accept that there are a wide range of personal views, and we urge respectful discourse on this matter, and that sports consider their duty of care to all athletes.'

text: River construirá un predio en San Martín de los Andes para hacer las pretemporadas La entidad de Núñez realizó en varias ocasiones la preparación física en la localidad de la provincia de Neuquén. River anunció que construirá un predio exclusivo en San Martín de los Andes, Neuquén, para que el primer equipo pueda realizar las pretemporadas. La noticia fue anunciada por el presidente de la entidad, Jorge Brito, quien aprovechó la ocasión de la cena solidaria para manifestar que "es un gran orgullo" la nueva infraestructura que construirá el cuadro de Núñez. “Hoy les quería contar detalles de una cosa que me pasó. Estaba en una reunión con miembros de la Comisión Directiva y Mariano Taratuty (encargado de las obras del club) me cuenta que habíamos cerrado un acuerdo en el que veníamos trabajando hace mucho tiempo, en la provincia de Neuquén", inició Brito sobre el tema. “Se trata del Chapelco Golf & Resort, donde vamos a tener un predio de pretemporada para el verano. Nos aportaron las tierras y nosotros vamos a hacer los campos de juego. Esto demuestra lo que logramos con el apoyo de todos, de empresarios, personas y socios, es algo que para mí es un gran orgullo”, destacó. El lugar donde River construirá el predio para las pretemporadas no es algo nuevo, ya que a principios de 2020, el equipo de Marcelo Gallardo llevó a cabo su preparación en en San Martín de Los Andes entre el 4 y 10 de enero. Las prácticas se llevaron a cabo en el estadio Municipal de Junín de Los Andes en esa ocasión. Además, es recordada porque posteriormente llegó un semestre atípico debido a la pandemia de coronavirus que azotó al mundo. Esto se repitió dos años después, cuando debido a cuestiones de salud pública, se decidió suspender el viaje a Estados Unidos y se realizó la pretemporada del 10 al 18 de enero en San Martín de los Andes. El plantel se alojó en Hotel Loi Suites Chapelco y realizó los entrenamientos en el predio El Desafío Mountain Resort. (NA).

text: [NHL](../) Germany Suffers First Defeat at 2024 WJC in Loss to Sweden After a [historic 4-3 win over Team Finland](//www.iihf.com/en/events/2024/wm20/gamecenter/playbyplay/42158/6-fin-vs-ger) on Dec. 27, Team Germany played host nation Team Sweden in their second game of the 2024 IIHF World Junior Championship (WJC) on Thursday, Dec. 28. Germany stayed in the game for most of it, but a dominant third period by Sweden gave the Germans a huge loss, as it ended 5-0. Germany Lost in a Close Game Coming off beating Finland for the first time at the WJC, there was a chance that Germany could come out slow in the second game in back-to-back days. However, with the help of netminder [Matthias Bittner](//www.eliteprospects.com/player/580513/matthias-bittner), Germany proved that yesterday was not a fluke despite the loss. Even after giving up 18 shots to Sweden compared to their six in the first period, there seemed to be a chance for Germany to get the equalizer. Related: [2024 Guide to the World Junior Championship](//thehockeywriters.com/2024-world-junior-championship-guide/) Otto Stenberg scored the lone goal for Sweden in the first period to give the hosts a lead at the 15:28 mark. That should be a good sign for the Germans; holding off the Swedes for that long shows that they played strong defensively for the first 20 minutes of the game. The second period seemed to be better for Germany, as they held Sweden to seven shots compared to their six, like in the first period. To be able to lessen Sweden’s chances seemed to give Germany more confidence as the game went on. [Julian Lutz](//thehockeywriters.com/docs/julian-lutz/) led the way in the shots department for Germany, getting six shots throughout the game. Coming into the 2024 WJC, it was clear that he was one of the players to watch. However, Sweden doubled their lead after a goal from Mattias Havelid, who ripped a slapshot in the top left corner of the net. It was almost the identical shot placement that Stenberg had in the previous period. Related: [Team Germany Players to Watch at 2024 WJC](//thehockeywriters.com/team-germany-players-to-watch-2024-world-junior-championship/) Germany went into the second intermission only down by two and still had a shot to claw back into the game despite being outshot 25-12. But going into the final frame, it was all Sweden in the third period to put this game away. Here Comes Otto Stenberg The third period saw Stenberg just put on an absolute clinic as he scored two more goals for Team Sweden in the third period to complete his hat trick. He scored both of his goals less than three minutes apart. The game was 2-0, and within a blink of an eye, it was 4-0 for Sweden because of Stenberg. Germany got outshot in the third period, 16-3, in a dominant period for the host nation. Noah Ostlund joined the scoring parry, giving Sweden the 5-0 lead, which was the last goal of the game. Sweden ended up outshooting Germany 41-15 in the game. Related: [3 Takeaways from Germany’s Upset Win Over Finland](//thehockeywriters.com/3-takeaways-from-germanys-upset-win-over-finland/) Latest News & Highlights Bittner could only do so much for Germany, as Sweden has been projected to finish second in this WJC, but he did manage to stop 36 of 41 shots that he faced. To only give up five goals to a team like Sweden is some silver lining compared to other games in the tournament so far. It was known that it would be a hard road for [Germany in this 2024 WJC](//www.deb-online.de/team/u20-nationalmannschaft/). Chance to Make Out of Group Stage Despite the loss, Germany is still in a good spot in Group A play after two games into the 2024 WJC. Their upset win over Finland has them in third place in the group ahead of the Finns and Team Latvia, and have a minus-4 goal differential after both of their games. Sign up for our NHL Prospects & Draft Substack newsletter The first four teams in each group move onto the quarter-final stage. That means if Germany can beat Latvia, they have a chance to get out of the group stage and possibly finish better or at least tie their eighth-place finish from the 2023 WJC. Entering the 2024 WJC, not a lot of experts thought Germany would place well in the tournament. However, they are in a good place to do so, even if their group includes Canada, Sweden, and Finland. Advancing out of the group is huge for Germany, as they’re looking to build up their stock in international tournaments. It will be interesting if Germany goes back to Philipp Dietl, who secured the 4-3 win for Germany over Finland. If not, will they look at Bittner after trying to keep the Germans in the game against the Swedes? Only time will tell when the puck drop rolls around in a couple of days. Their next game is Saturday, Dec. 30 versus Latvia at 1:30 p.m. eastern on NHL Network. text: West Ham beat Arsenal 2-0 at the Emirates in an incredibly frustrating match for the Gunners. Mikel Arteta’s side bossed the game but couldn’t seem to find a way through. The Hammers, on the other hand, scored a fluke goal off a ball that almost certainly went out of play and from a corner where the header hit the cross bar and post before bouncing in. You could play that exact match 100 times and I think Arsenal lose it once, maybe twice. They draw it 7 or 8 times. And they win 90 of ‘em. Arsenal really can’t afford to be dropping points at home if they want to challenge for the Premier League title. It especially shouldn’t happen against David Moyes, who until tonight, hadn’t managed a team to a win at a Big Six opponent in 72 tries. Nor should it happen against West Ham, who had just 2 wins in their last 30 matches at Arsenal. The Gunners really need to be taking at least a point at the Emirates and probably all three. There will be plenty of overreaction to today’s match and it will be misguided. The sky isn’t falling. The team is just going through a rough patch with some (especially) bad luck. Putting aside whether the ball stayed in play, West Ham only score their opening goal because a cross to nobody in particular gets cut out by an Arsenal defender and the clearance goes straight into his teammate. That’s just unfortunate. Arsenal fired 30 shots today, 8 on target. They had 77 touches inside West Ham’s box. They failed to convert five big chances. Statistically, they were more likely to score five goals than zero today. Gabriel Jesus twice headed over the bar from promising positions. Bukayo Saka hit the post. On another night, any number of those go in and we’re having a totally different conversation. Gabriel Martinelli is undoubtedly in the midst of a dry spell and a dip in form. He’s still involved and threatening, but he’s missing his cutting edge. He’s dribbling into bad spots, misplacing passes, and needs to adjust his shooting radar. Continuing to do what he’s doing is probably the best way for him to break out of the slump. Leandro Trossard was dreadful. He’s been consistently great as a substitute for Arsenal but has struggled when he’s had to start. The Gunners really missed Kai Havertz, who was suspended because of a soft 5th yellow card. His size in the box and physicality might have made the difference. Martin Ødegaard was magnificent. Whatever Mikel Arteta said to him / switched up in his usage or responsibilities (or maybe it’s just that he’s fully healthy), he is a dominant, creative force once again. Hopefully he maintains that form. The Gunners also had two “you’ve seen them given” penalty shouts not given — Gabriel Jesus getting taken out by a sliding Tomas Soucek in the first half, Bukayo Saka getting tripped / going over in the second. The Gabriel Jesus one was almost certainly a penalty — it was a carbon copy of a foul correctly called against Oleksandr Zinchenko for sliding in on Vladimir Coufal earlier in the half. Soucek slide through, was nowhere near the ball, and clattered into the Arsenal attacker. I’d guess it wasn’t given because 1) it was in the box and 2) Gabriel Jesus doesn’t get to the ball, but neither of those are reasons to not call a foul a foul. I’d say the Saka incident was 60-40, maybe 70-30, against being a penalty. Now, if you’ll permit me a bit of a rant. West Ham’s first goal demonstrates a fundamental problem with VAR. There is zero chance the linesman, who had to see through two posts and multiple bodies, in a split second whether the ball went over the end line, has any idea if it did. The same can be said for Michael Oliver — he’s not in a position to make any kind of determination and he shouldn’t be, as the center referee. In that case, they are supposed to make their best guess as to what the correct call is, but in reality, they just don’t make a call and let it go to VAR. The problem with letting it go to VAR is that what was, at best a guess at what happened, and at worst, a total non-call, creates a presumption that must be overcome to rule out the goal. The ball looked like it went out. The best evidence is that the ball was out. There is a clear shot where, I believe, if the ball was in play, you’d be able to see it beyond Jarrod Bowen’s leg and / or overlapping the post. You can’t see it because it’s almost certainly out. That doesn’t matter, however, because we’ve set up the system in such a way as to give deference where it shouldn’t be given. In instances where the referee cannot say what happened, which they can tell the VAR over the communication system, they should be reviewing the decision anew. But that’s my gripe with how VAR operates. Under the rules as written, you can understand and explain the VAR outcome today. It’s the second time this season that Arsenal have had a goal scored against them when there wasn’t enough to definitively show the ball was out of play. If the linesman raises his flag and signals for a goal kick, the goal doesn’t get given by VAR. The same can be said for the goal in the [Newcastle](https://cominghomenewcastle.sbnation.com) match. It’s wild that in the richest league in the world, with cameras everywhere, we can’t do better. The technology to automate the call and get it right every time exists, too. They used it at the World Cup. The Premier League, for whatever reason, has declined to implement it. Slash end rant. It’s incredibly frustrating because goals change games. There is no getting around that. So when you have a goal, especially an opening one, that probably shouldn’t have counted, you’ve got an unwarranted shift in the entire tenor of the match. But there isn’t much that can be done about that. The goal counted, rightly or wrongly, so Arsenal have to respond. And they didn’t do a good enough job of it. At least not from the only standpoint that matters to the result — putting the ball in the net. But I can point to any number of graphics that show that Arsenal played fine, even quite well, and it just didn’t go their way. Check out [Scott Willis’ postmatch stats tweets](https://twitter.com/scottjwillis). David Raya saved an “oh by the way” penalty just as the match ended. Well done to him. That’s sorta how I feel about today’s match overall. A big old shrug. It happened. It’s a bummer of a result and it definitely hurts the title challenge, but it’s not a reason to make massive changes. Arsenal are playing winning football and sometimes you don’t win when you should. On to the next.

text: New Delhi: One doesn't have to look beyond Rohit Sharma's post-match comments, while carrying out a post-mortem examination of India's abject surrender by an innings and 32 runs in the first Test against South Africa in Centurion on Thursday. “If we have to win Test matches, we have to come together collectively and we didn’t do that. We didn’t exploit the conditions with the ball and then again didn’t show up today with the bat,” Rohit summed up India's performance perfectly after the end of the match on Thursday. India lost inside three days suffering batting failures in both the innings and unable to break through the South African batting line-up like the home team did against them at SuperSport Park. Traditionally a pace-favouring track, India were up against it after losing the toss and being sent into bat. For a team that has never won a Test series in South Africa in 30 years, countering the venom of a pace attack led by Kagiso Rabada proved to be too much for the much-vaunted Indian batters. Woeful batting In away conditions, particularly in the bouncy tracks of South Africa, Indian batters have historically failed to put up much fight. Judged by the yardstick, they didn't fare much poorer. But with India being the financial hub of the game and its star batters all being dubbed superstars of the modern era all exposed to away conditions, a little bit of application and gumption was expected. Their produced a performance that had anything but. Flat-track bullies at their own backyard, they had creases on their forehead once the ball began to seam and swing, poking at deliveries outside the off stump to offer catching practice to the slip fielders or judging the line incorrectly to have their defences breached. Only KL Rahul though his 101 in the first innings and Virat Kohli with his 76 in the second displayed the courage and determination to stay at the crease and survive under testing conditions. The others led by skipper Rohit Sharma were simply all at sea on how to do it. Rabada dismissed him twice, cleverly utilising the short ball to exploit his propensity to pull uppishly in the first innings and then poked at his suspect footwork in the second to have him bowled. It showed how much homework the Proteans did dismiss the Indians. As for the others like Yashshvi Jaiswal, Shreyas Iyer and Shubman Gill, they need to learn quickly and understand that batting abroad in Test cricket is a different challenge to inflicting misery on the bowlers in the IPL. With questionable batting techniques, how much they can offer at Newlands, where India have never won a Test, needs to be seen. They need to leave their big-hitting tendencies behind in the locker room and respect the conditions a bit more, taking cue from Rahul and Kohli. Inexperienced bowling Even before India had lost on Thursday, Indian commentators had begun blaming Indian bowlers for unable to restrict South Africa to anywhere near 245 that the visiting team put up thanks to Rahul's 101. They conveniently side stepped India's poor batting performance. While it's true that once India had conceded a 163-run lead, it was always going to be difficult for India in the second innings, but too conveniently blame 'soft target' Prasidh Krishna for his unimpressive performance is a bit too much. Even star bowlers Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj weren't potent enough and with India's best all-format bowler Mohammed Shami absent with injury undoubtedly their bowling attack was weak. Rohit Sharma would have expected a bit more penetration from his pacers and fast-bowling all-rounder Shardul Thakur. But even in helpful conditions they weren't up to the mark, giving away too many runs. Elgar's last dance In his farewell series, Dean Elgar unleashed a different side to his batting that people were hitherto unfamiliar with. Normally a stodgy Test opener who backs his tight defence and unwavering concentration levels to bat for long hours, Elgar batted far more freely. He had a secret desire of scoring his first Test ton at his home ground and who knew he had saved it for his last appearance at the SuperSport Park. Elgar didn't try fancy shots or tried to flirt outside the off stump. But judged the loose deliveries correctly and dispatched them without fail. Equally importantly the 36-year-old guided his younger batting partners Tony de Zorzi, David Bedingham and Marco Jansen on how to bat, producing valuable partnerships that took the match away from India.

text: Liam Lawson reflects on the disappointment of missing out on a fulltime F1 seat. Credits: Image - Getty, video - Newshub You can't always get what you want... Alex Powell - Liam Lawson misses out on a Formula One seat, again When Daniel Ricciardo broke his hand in practice for Formula One's Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, Kiwi hopeful Liam Lawson's life changed forever. Already embedded with Red Bull as reserve driver for its two teams, Lawson jumped into the cockpit and didn't take a backwards step. Driving for AlphaTauri, Lawson impressed from his first race, notched the team's then-best result of the season and even knocked Red Bull stablemate Max Verstappen out of qualifying in Singapore. Liam Lawson. Photo credit: Getty Images Only guaranteed a drive until Ricciardo recovered, Lawson's results became too hard to ignore, but motorsport politics denied the Kiwi a fulltime drive in 2024, as the commercial appeal of Ricciardo and Japan's Yuki Tsunoda saw them both re-signed for next season. In September, Newshub revealed that those contracts were signed before he'd even jumped in the car, leaving Lawson, 21, to continue as reserve next season. Make no mistake, it's when and not if Lawson returns to Formula One as a fulltime driver. Will Hewett - Football Ferns fail to fire at World Cup This might seem harsh to many, but the NZ women are my disappointment of the sporting year. They had a real opportunity to set the benchmark for women's football in this country, when the FIFA Women's World Cup arrived on our shores. It all started so well, with an upset over Norway in the tournament's opening game giving New Zealand their first victory at a senior World Cup. From there, things went downhill, as they lost to the Philippines - the only team ranked below them in their group - and drawing with Switzerland to see them bundled out of the tournament. The side made unwanted history by becoming the first host of a Women's Football World Cup not to make it to the knockout stage. Yes, there were so many positives to come from the tournament, but their results didn't match. Hannah Wilkinson. Photo credit: Photosport They had the opportunity to transfix a nation, just like the Matildas did in Australia, which could've propelled women's football in New Zealand to another level. Grant Chapman - Social media bullying of rugby referees Any referees, for that matter. Wouldn't it be nice for a losing team to walk off the field with their heads held high, and NOT grizzle about how they were robbed by the refs or umpires or TMO or VAR? Wouldn't it be great if bandwagon fans could resist the temptation to share their toxic misinformation on social media? We only have to look at the fallout from the Rugby World Cup final, when All Blacks supporters rekindled their hatred for ref Wayne Barnes, who had apparently robbed them 15 years ago with a non-call that probably belonged to his linesmen anyway. That's a whole generation ago. Then the third match official copped it for having too big an influence on the game. Wayne Barnes issues a yellow card during the Rugby World Cup final. Photo credit: Getty Images While coach Ian Foster deserves respect for his work with the All Blacks over the past 12 months, the moaning from their camp after losing to South Africa did them no credit. Our own Super Rugby Pacific final was no better, with losing Chiefs coaching Clayton McMillan passively-agressively refusing to blame ref Ben O'Keeffe, but tacitly endorsing the crowd's booing of officials at post-game presentations. At least give McMillan credit for checking on O'Keeffe's mental health afterwards. Good teams and good coaches take officials out of the equation by dominating their opponents. If you can't do that, you should simply learn to live with the result. Sullivan Harnett - Silver Ferns' worst World Cup I can't go past the Silver Ferns. I'd thrown some money on them to win the tournament at the start, but they did not live up to those expectations in South Africa. A draw with the hosts, then three straight losses to miss out on a medal at the World Cup, just was not good enough. Dame Noeline Taurua coaching at the Netball World Cup. Photo credit: Photosport Yes, they did bounce back with wins later in the year, beating Australia and narrowly losing the Constellation Cup, but not winning your pinnacle event must make the year a disappointment. Stephen Foote - Black Ferns Last year, the Black Ferns had the world at their feet. The people's champions were the unanimous selection as Team of the Year, after their hometown heroics at the Rugby World Cup, winning the final in highly dramatic fashion and turning the nation into women's rugby experts. Turn the page to 2023 and it's a much different story. The transition from saviour Sir Wayne Smith to new coach Allan Bunting has been fraught, to put it kindly. The freewheeling expansive style under Sir Wayne has disappeared, as has any momentum garnered from their Cup exploits, with a lacklustre showing at the inaugural WXV1. They whiffed on their chance to consolidate their crown by limping to defeat against France and being put to the sword in a World Cup final rematch against England. England's Abby Dow leaves the Black Ferns defence grasping at air. Photo credit: Photosport Sure, they recorded some lopsided wins over Australia, but let's face it, Australia are terrible, as are every other team beneath the gulf that separates the top three from the rest of the global pack. Success next year will be critical to ensuring that wave of goodwill surrounding the women's game doesn’t fizzle out with minimal fanfare. Tia McDougall - Silver Ferns The defending champions finished fourth at the Netball World Cup, their worst result ever. The team that went was incredibly talented and it was off the back of a highly competitive ANZ Premiership season that saw some incredible skill showcased, but for some reason fell flat. Nothing clicked. I know it was a major blow when Grace Nweke suffered an injury, but at World Cup level, it's not good enough to build your team around one player. Grant Chapman - Blues Can we please stop referring to their match-up against the Crusaders as a 'rivalry'? Sure, the Auckland-based Super Rugby side claimed the only crown to elude the South Island juggernaut over the past seven years - the hit-and-giggle trans-Tasman contest during COVID-19 - but even we Aucklanders don't count that as a real thing. During Leon MacDonald's tenure as coach, the Blues have been bullish about their massive improvement and how another Super Rugby title is just around the corner - two decades after their most recent. Marcel Renata reflects on the Blues' semi-final defeat to Crusaders. Photo credit: Photosport When they finally beat the Crusaders in 2022, before falling in the final, they actually seemed on the verge of a breakthrough. Their most recent encounter was a 52-15 drubbing in this year's semis suggests they are as far away from their next title as they ever were. Perhaps the only glimmer of hope comes from Scott Robertson's promotion to the All Blacks job, taking MacDonald with him. That should level the playingfield somewhat.
